_comment: #5576 (2026-11-09): the Hevy title no longer reads this file first — routine_title.build_title_context reads the weekly phase evaluator's PHASE#STATE row (#5575; title + since = the recorded TRANSITION date) and falls back to `current`/`current_started` here only while no STATE row exists or it cannot be read. The evaluator seeds its first STATE from these two fields; the site reader (lambdas/web/site_api_data.py) still reads `current`. Advance the phase through manage_training_phase (override), not by editing this file. Original note: Ordered training phases for Hevy routine titles (Phase - Type - N - Y), consumed by routine_title.build_title_context. Manually advanced by Matthew — no auto/milestone-driven transitions. `current` is the active phase; flip it to advance and bump `current_started` to that date (this resets N per type). `current_started` = phase_started_date: N counts PERFORMED workouts of each type on/after it (inclusive). A phase may deliberately span experiment cycles, so the reset does NOT touch these two fields. See ADR-067 / ADR-088 (2026-06-16 work order) and the 2026-09-07 #3671 amendment.
_y_anchor_note: There is deliberately no `reset_epoch_date` here (#3671). The Y counter — performed workouts since the experiment began — is DERIVED from EXPERIMENT_START_DATE in lambdas/common/constants.py, which every reset regenerates and which ships in every bundle. The hand-maintained copy that used to live here survived eleven resets stuck at 2026-06-16, and since this file is not staged into the Lambda bundle the runtime read the S3 copy, so re-anchoring the repo copy did not move the live counter. tests/test_routine_title_y_anchor_3671.py fails if the field is reintroduced.
